newsitem.title: ESTONIA: TALLINN APPROVES WATER COMPANY SELLOFF.
newsitem.headline: TALLINN APPROVES WATER COMPANY SELLOFF.

text.p: Tallinn city government on Friday approved the restructuring plan of the Tallinn Water and Sewage Company, including 66 percent of its shares to be sold, city government officials said.
"The sale will involve a large sum of money and it seems that investors and interest groups are interested," Tallinn deputy mayor, Ants Leemets, told Reuters.
He declined to name the groups who have shown interest.
"The first step is to form a joint-stock company and then decide how to sell the shares," Leemets added.
The municipal company is to be formed into a joint-stock company with share capital of 865.79 million kroons and all of the shares held by city government.
The board of the joint-stock company will be responsible for taking the company's shares to the stock exchange, Leemets said.
"I do not want to forecast but it seems to me that it will be taken to the stock exchange relatively quickly," he said.
The city government decision is still to be discussed and approved by the city council.
